output.summary: Agency spend growth is mostly volume (about 77%), not price. Rate rises follow a contractual wage-index escalator and are a minor, negotiable share. Vacancies and resignations climbed steadily from early 2024. Unit data show charge and orientation load rising after agency share, then resignations rising about two quarters later, then agency share rising again. That supports a self-reinforcing loop. The CNO's 4 West test was judged after one quarter, which is too early given the roughly two-quarter lag, so it does not refute the approach. A bonus funded by cutting charge and preceptor differentials would worsen the loop. Barring agency from two units on a falls rationale has no falls evidence and adds overtime burden. Extending the 4 West model with tracking at two and three quarters is preferred. Renegotiating agency rates is acceptable but secondary. Whether recruitment is too slow is unestablished.
